## Dissent from the `domain:services` seat — ⛔ not claiming; the fix lands in `packages/core`, which is the engine lane

`domain:services` seat, session `session_0157mMVAq9fjGe2kaSD2aJC8`, round 1. `pm:retriage` hung in the same stroke as this comment. ⛔ No `domain:*` touched, no assignee taken, `pm:queue` left in place — routing has a single producer and it is not this seat.

This card came up as a live dispatch candidate this round (it is the lane's only ruled, unblocked, non-trivial queue card). It stopped at the **measurement**, not at a file conflict.

### What I measured, on `origin/main` @ `27b6902`

The triage grading reads *"caching successful localization reads of `sys_setting` … lands in the settings/localization service layer — `domain:services`."* The localization **read** does not live in a service package:

| the thing | where it actually is | lane by the anchoring rule |
|---|---|---|
| the function that would hold the cache — `resolveLocalizationContext` | **`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:819`** | `domain:engine` |
| the precedent this card is explicitly the sibling of — #10221's **failure-only** memo | same file (`packages/core` CHANGELOG: *"`resolveLocalizationContext` now memoizes a FAILED read's fallback per `(ql, tenantId, userId)` for 30s (#10221)"*) | `domain:engine` |
| the invalidation source — the "settings change bus" | `SettingsService.subscribe()` / `onChange()`, `packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts:751` | `domain:services` |
| the "engine-seam backstop on `sys_setting` writes" | engine seam | `domain:engine` |

⚠️ **Naming note for whoever grades this**: there is **no module called a "settings change bus"** — repo-wide, `settingsChangeBus` / `SettingsChangeBus` / `settings-change-bus` return **zero** hits. The design's term maps to the `subscribers` set on `SettingsService` (`:570-571`, dispatch at `:763-769`, public seam at `:751` and `onChange` at `:1454-1469`). Reverse control: that file is 2586 lines and the `subscribe` greps returned real hits, so the zero is a real zero. A dispatch that tells a dev to "subscribe to the settings change bus" will send them looking for a module that does not exist.

### Why this is a routing question and not a hot-file question

The card's **centre of mass is in `packages/core`** — the cache, the identity pin ("cached answer ≡ uncached answer"), and the interaction with #10221's existing memo (the card's own hard constraint: *"the two must not fight"*) are all in one engine-lane function. `domain:services` owns the invalidation **source** and nothing else.

Per the anchoring rule, `domain:*` is *the package where the fix lands*, so on the dominant-landing reading this is `domain:engine`. But it is genuinely two-lane, so I am putting the fork to triage rather than asserting one:

| | shape | who dispatches |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | Re-route to **`domain:engine`** — the cache and its pin are core's; the `SettingsService.subscribe()` call is a thin consumer touch the same PR carries | engine seat |
| **B** | Keep here, formally as a **cross-domain exception** — the skill's cross-domain path requires triage to *name* the lane PM, and the claim then declares the full file surface and runs the directed in-flight check | this seat, on triage's word |
| **C** | Split contract-first: engine lands the cache seam + identity pin, services lands the invalidation subscription behind a `Blocked-by:` | both, serialized |

⭐ **My recommendation is A**, on the strength of the #10221 precedent: the failure-cache and the success-cache are the *same memo in the same function*, and splitting them across two lanes is how they end up fighting — which is precisely the failure the card's own text warns about.

⚠️ Against A, honestly: the hard acceptance requirement is *"invalidation must be **synchronous in-process**"*, and the only thing that can fire that invalidation is the services-side subscriber. An engine-lane dev will need to reach into `service-settings` for the wiring. If triage judges that reach to be the bigger half, **B** is defensible and I will take it.

### One thing the next dispatch must carry either way

The card says *"design measured at `992161b728`; re-verify cited seams on current `origin/main` before implementing"* — and it is right to. The acceptance test it names, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/analytics-timezone.dogfood.test.ts`, **does exist** (verified). ⛔ But the "settings change bus" phrasing above must be corrected in the dispatch text, or the dev burns a cycle hunting a module that was never there.

### What this seat did and did not do

⛔ No label removed, no `domain:*` changed, no assignee taken. `pm:retriage` added alongside `pm:queue` (they coexist by design), which also takes the card out of this lane's dispatch selection until it is graded — a card with an open routing objection is not dispatchable.

This card was graded `domain:services`, the services seat **dissented with measurements** rather than claiming it, and triage **accepted the dissent and re-routed to `domain:engine`** (shape A, comment `5421154211`): the cache, the identity pin, and the must-not-fight interaction with #10221's failure memo are one engine-lane function; the `SettingsService` wiring is a thin consumer touch carried in the same PR. ⛔ Option C (contract-first split across lanes) was **rejected on the ground that splitting the two memos across lanes is how they end up fighting**. ⛔ Option B (cross-domain exception) unnecessary once the label is right.

### The ruled design — ⛔ not re-adjudicable

Provenance: design = #11633 comment `5394942824` (§4 leg C, §10.1); maintainer acceptance = #11633 comment `5404681591`, 2026-08-25, verbatim, ⛔ untranslated:

> 接受你的建议，继续

with forks **1A / 2B / 3A / TTL-0**. This is **leg C, ship-first**.

**Hard requirement carried from the design's re-measurement**: invalidation must be **synchronous in-process**. ⛔ A TTL alone, or deferred invalidation, does **not** satisfy it — `analytics-timezone.dogfood.test.ts` is this leg's acceptance test for "write-invalidation primary" precisely because it observes read-after-write.

**Acceptance criterion**: that test passes against the cached path, **plus** a "cached answer ≡ uncached answer" identity pin per design §7.

### 🚨 The correction triage ordered carried into this dispatch

⛔ **There is NO module called a "settings change bus."** The design document's phrase maps to nothing in the tree. Measured on current `origin/main`:

```
settingsChangeBus / settings-change-bus, repo-wide  → 0
CONTROL (fires): settings-service.ts:751  subscribe(
                 settings-service.ts:1447 onChange(handler: SettingsChangeHandler)
```

The real seam is `SettingsService.subscribe()` / `onChange()` in `packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts`. ⛔ A dispatch that said "subscribe to the settings change bus" would send you hunting a module that never existed — this text says the real name instead, which is the whole reason triage ordered the correction.

### Premises — measured by me on `origin/main` after PR #12652 landed, controls included

- `resolveLocalizationContext` exported at `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:819`.
- The **#10221 failure-only memo lives in the same file** (6 hits). ⚠️ The card's own hard constraint is that the success-cache and the failure-memo **must not fight** — they are the same memo in the same function, so read #10221's machinery before adding a second one.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/analytics-timezone.dogfood.test.ts` **exists** (1).
- ⚠️ The card says "design measured at `992161b728`; re-verify cited seams on current `origin/main`" — and `origin/main` has moved since, including the authz substrate that landed minutes before this claim.

⛔ **Confirm or refute every one of these before writing code.** They are my readings, not yours, and a premise in a brief carries the same burden as a claim in a review. `premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is a legitimate delivery.

**Addendum — docs-drift close-out on PR #12694.** Read at PR head `cdf400ea`. **Nothing was edited; no commit was added; the PR is unchanged and still draft.** Verdicts below rest on opening each page, not on the bot's silence or the PM's read.

### Negative control, which decides how to read the 3 rows

Repo-wide over `content/`, **zero** hits for `resolveLocalizationContext`, `localizationSettingsState`, `writeEpoch`. No hand-written page names any symbol this diff introduces or changes. `expiresAt` was therefore the only identifier the bot could match on — and it is the single most collision-prone name in the diff, since it is also the field name for every token/session/link expiry in the product.

### The 3 bot rows — all FALSE, with the reason per page

| page | what its `expiresAt` actually is | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx` | two client-SDK call params: `client.keys.create({ …, expiresAt })` (API-key expiry, line 472) and `client.shareLinks.create(…, { expiresAt })` (share-link expiry, line 478) | FALSE — a wall-clock expiry a caller *supplies*; this diff neither reads nor writes either |
| `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx` | `AuthSession.expiresAt: string`, documented in-line as "Session expiry (ISO 8601)" (line 149) | FALSE — an ISO-8601 string on the session contract; the cache field is a numeric ms deadline on a process-local entry |
| `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` | better-auth's camelCase→snake_case schema mapping: `session: { fields: { expiresAt: 'expires_at' } }` and the same for `sys_verification` (lines 1203, 1205) | FALSE — a column-name mapping table for persisted auth rows |

None of the three describes the localization read path, a cache, or a TTL. The bot is precision-first and says a wrong row is reportable, so recording these as wrong is the useful output.

### The blind spot, worked by hand — a page that states the rule by its inputs

Swept `content/docs/` for freshness/caching/immediacy prose attached to settings, localization, timezone, locale or currency, and separately for any page asserting a TTL or staleness contract over a settings read. Pages opened and cleared:

- ⭐ `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx` — **the real near-miss, and the reason this sweep was worth doing.** Line 180 states a freshness rule behaviourally and names none of my symbols: *"For code that reads the same namespace repeatedly, `createClient()` keeps a snapshot that refreshes on every `settings:changed` event."* **Still true.** That documents `SettingsService.createClient()`'s own snapshot; this diff adds an independent second subscriber to the same seam and changes neither `createClient`, its snapshot, nor the event. It corroborates the design rather than contradicting it — the page already documents `settings:changed` as *the* established freshness mechanism, which is the seam leg C's primary invalidation uses.
- `content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx` — two hits, both cleared: the "immediately" at line 555 is pinyin-search companion columns for `sys_user`, and the bucketing callout at line 669 describes the **explicit `timezone` parameter** on `ObjectQL.aggregate`, a different route from the analytics-dataset path that resolves a workspace default. No claim about read freshness.
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx` — same: `timezone` as a per-call `aggregate()` argument.
- `content/docs/references/system/settings-manifest.mdx` — contains no caching or freshness language at all.
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx` — this PR's own edit, and the **only** page in the tree that states a TTL/staleness contract over a settings read. It already carries both halves the ruling cares about: that invalidation is synchronous and in-process, and that the TTL bounds only what neither seam can see.

⇒ **No page is falsified by this change, and no docs edit is in scope.** The one page that states the rule behaviourally states it about a different consumer and remains accurate.

### Scope

⛔ No code changed, no test changed, no doc changed, no commit added. `packages/core/src/security/index.ts` still never opened — the fence holds. PR #12694 remains **draft**, not enqueued, auto-merge not enabled. Terminal report `5437435119` stands unamended; `status` stays `done`, `out_of_scope_findings` stays empty.

**① The serial fence held.** `packages/core/src/security/index.ts` is **absent from the changed-file list**. That was the one real collision risk I fenced (the retirement family owns that barrel this round), and it is clean.

**② Clause-② `no` is verifiable, not asserted.** Every new symbol in the diff — `LOCALIZATION_CACHE_TTL_ENV`, `localizationSuccessCacheTtlMs`, `readWriteEpoch`, `LocalizationSettingsState`, `localizationSettingsState`, `LocalizationCacheEntry`, `localizationEntryIsLive`, `putLocalizationEntry` — is declared **without `export`**.
